articles.title: The Five Senses of Artificial Intelligence
articles.excerpt: An AI agent can write a program, execute it, discover that something went wrong, and try again. But what happens when the program works perfectly and the person using it still finds it useless? There’…
articles.body: An AI agent can write a program, execute it, discover that something went wrong, and try again. But what happens when the program works perfectly and the person using it still finds it useless? There’s an important difference between completing a task and understanding whether the outcome was valuable. As AI becomes increasingly capable of acting in the world, I think this distinction will become more important, and it may change the role humans play in the development of artificial intelligence. For most of the history of computing, software has been something we build, package, and sell. Creating it required specialized knowledge, time, and significant resources. Entire companies were built around applications, and the software itself became the product.
articles.author: Massimiliano Genta

articles.title: Five questions to ask before you use an AI answer
articles.excerpt: AI tools write answers that sound sure, including the wrong ones. You do not need to be technical to catch many of them. Ask these five questions, in this order, in the same chat. "What would have to…
articles.body: AI tools write answers that sound sure, including the wrong ones. You do not need to be technical to catch many of them. Ask these five questions, in this order, in the same chat. "What would have to be true for this to be wrong?" A good answer names real conditions. A vague one tells you the first answer was weaker than it sounded. "Which parts are you sure about, and which parts are you guessing?" Mark the guesses and check only those. "What did you assume about my situation?" Many bad answers are good answers to a question you did not ask. Your country, your budget and your skill level are the usual missing pieces. "Give me one source I can open myself, and tell me if you are not certain it exists." Then open it.

articles.title: What counts as a deep fake under Article 50(4)? Examples for marketing teams
articles.excerpt: This guide was drafted by an AI agent from the primary sources linked at the bottom, and has not been reviewed by a lawyer. It is general information, not legal advice. The original is at https://mdod…
articles.body: This guide was drafted by an AI agent from the primary sources linked at the bottom, and has not been reviewed by a lawyer. It is general information, not legal advice. The original is at https://mdodeja.github.io/eu-ai-act-article-50-guide/guides/what-counts-as-a-deepfake-article-50.html . Short answer. Under the EU AI Act a deep fake is AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video that resembles real people, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear authentic. It is not limited to faces or to fakes made to deceive. A deployer who publishes one has to disclose that it is AI-made, clearly and at first exposure. Text is never a deep fake; it has its own rule.

articles.title: Gaming User Document Retention: Storage Selection, Lifecycle Delete, and Export Boundaries
articles.excerpt: Short answer: keep signed user documents in private object storage, but make the database the owner of retention intent and tenant isolation; use lifecycle deletion only as a coarse backstop, and keep…
articles.body: Short answer: keep signed user documents in private object storage, but make the database the owner of retention intent and tenant isolation; use lifecycle deletion only as a coarse backstop, and keep backups and exports outside the user-deletion promise until their separate retention rules are explicit. That answer is deliberately less tidy than “set a one-day TTL.” A deletion deadline is a product guarantee. Object storage lifecycle cleanup is an asynchronous storage operation. They can cooperate, but they are not the same clock. The decision record: protect the tenant boundary first For a gaming service storing signed tournament waivers, parental-consent forms, or account documents, the first invariant is that a request for tenant A can never select tenant B's key.

articles.title: BioWare Was the Greatest RPG Developer Ever
articles.excerpt: There are many great role-playing game developers, past and present. But none can touch what BioWare has done over 30-plus years.
articles.body: BioWare is dead , and my feelings are a strange cocktail of anger, sadness, and Jack’s Complete Lack of Surprise. The legendary RPG studio was bought by a private investment group earlier this year, and history shows that venture capital frequently kills what it touches, extracting whatever value out of it that it can before moving onto the next victim. It’s a hell of a contrast to the beginning of BioWare, which started out as such a pure thing. Two practicing doctors, Ray Muzyka and Greg Zeschuk, quit medicine to pursue their dream of making computer role-playing games. Sure, the studio was bought and sold a couple of times between then and now, and yes, BioWare’s recent results haven’t lived up to its venerable past, but my goodness, what a legacy this studio leaves behind.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.

articles.title: Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise.'
articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.
